title: Introduction to Natural Language Processing
weeklyTopics: Neural Networks and Neural Language Models
Sequence Labeling for POS and NER
skills: naive bayes and logistic regression classification
team research project and poster presentation
workloadNotes: 26 lectures (must complete lecture assignments for 20 to earn full credit; not accepted late); 10 lab assignments (lowest dropped, due weekly); 3 homework assignments (10%/day late penalty up to 3 days); a group "One Cool Thing" video presentation; one in-person exam (no final exam); and a semester-long team project (2-3 students) worth 30% total (5% proposal, 5% progress report, 15% final report, 5% poster), with a mandatory final poster session. Exact overall weights for lecture/lab/homework categories were not machine-readable from the source grading table.
prerequisitesText: Designed for junior/senior undergraduates in CS, information science, linguistics, or related fields; expected to write code proficiently (Python recommended) and have studied algorithms, probability, and statistics.
textbooks: Dan Jurafsky and James H. Martin, Speech and Language Processing, 3rd ed. draft (online)
